action: Authored plugins/pmcro-reflector/skills/reflect-and-seed/scripts/Test-QueueRootDerivation.ps1: a self-contained, deterministic Test-*.ps1-convention script (params -ReflectorScriptPath to target a specific copy of Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1, defaulting to the real one next to it, and -ScratchRoot to override the temp scratch location). It resolves sibling plugin scripts (New-Trail/New-OrchestrateFrame/New-PlanFrame/New-MakeStep/New-CheckFrame) relative to its own $PSScriptRoot, drives two minimal orchestrate->plan->make->check->reflect-and-seed cycles in a disposable temp folder -- Case A with an absolute custom -PmcroRoot, Case B reproducing the default relative '.\.pmcro' usage via Push-Location -- asserts (Test-Path) each queue item landed at the correct <root>/queue/ path, always deletes its scratch folder in-line (no try/finally needed for the delete since it runs unconditionally after both cases, but each case's own work is wrapped in try/catch so one case's exception doesn't abort the other), and exits 0 with a PASS message or 1 with a FAIL message naming which case broke. Smoke-tested it directly against the real, current Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1: exited 0 with the expected PASS message; confirmed by search that no queueroot-check artifacts leaked into the real .pmcro/trails or .pmcro/queue.

Confirmed Test-QueueRootDerivation.ps1 exits 0/PASS against the real, current Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1 (rerun, same result as step 1's smoke test). Then made a scratch copy of Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1, reverted only its QueueRoot line back to the pre-fix version, and ran the new script with -ReflectorScriptPath pointed at that reverted copy: it exited 1 (non-zero), as intended. It also surfaced a genuine, previously-undocumented detail about the original bug: Case A (absolute -PmcroRoot) failed the way already known and fixed (queue item mislands outside the repo); Case B (default relative -PmcroRoot) did NOT silently misland under the old code as my earlier Reflection assumed -- it actually threw a hard exception ('Cannot bind argument to parameter Path because it is an empty string' from Join-Path), because Split-Path-ing '.\.pmcro' down two parent levels yields an empty string, which Windows PowerShell 5.1's Join-Path refuses as a -Path argument. Verified this by hand outside the script too (direct Split-Path/Join-Path repro). This means the pre-fix bug had two distinct failure modes depending on how -PmcroRoot was supplied -- silent misplacement when absolute, hard crash when the literal relative default was ever actually exercised (which real prior usage apparently never did, since queue items already existed in the repo from before this session, and those were presumably filed with an explicit absolute -PmcroRoot, matching the silent-misplacement path, not the crash path). The already-shipped fix handles both correctly, confirmed by step 1 and the earlier fix cycle. Deleted the scratch reverted copy and its containing folder afterward; confirmed no queueroot-check artifacts leaked into the real .pmcro/trails or .pmcro/queue.
